title: Finnish moth community change was near its spatial warming benchmark in 1993-2022
abstract: We tested whether weak transfer of spatial temperature gradients also occurs in five Finnish monitoring groups with European species temperature indices. We used released community summaries and continuous GHCN-CAMS annual temperature at the survey sites. In 246 moth sites in 1993-2022, the community temperature index trend was 0.0126 C per year. This was 22% of the air temperature trend, but 1.02 times the change expected from the spatial community-temperature slope (95% spatial-block interval 0.86 to 1.24). The ratio was 1.02 after removal of a dominant cyclic moth species, 1.02 in long-running sites, and 0.99 to 1.08 when five-year blocks were omitted. Birds and butterflies had ratios of 0.29 and 0.38. Plant and phytoplankton point trends were negative. A separate exact decomposition showed that weather in the three plant survey years made the temperature trend 2.45 times the trend from the full annual record. Thus a small direct temperature ratio need not show a large deficit relative to spatial sorting. The moth result limits the general claim of weak space-for-time transfer. It does not identify a causal warming effect or a demographic mechanism. Intervals condition on survey years and fixed thermal indices; sites and periods differ among groups.

display.caption: A: CTI trend divided by the full annual temperature trend. B: the same ratio divided by the spatial CTI-temperature slope. Bars are 95% spatial-block intervals, conditional on survey years. Grey lines mark one; the orange line in B marks the prior pooled value of 0.12 for reference, not a matched control. C: temperature trends from survey years and from the full annual record.
